memory_lessons.applicability: For this fixed 128-thread geometry, comparing the inter-warp combination separately from the warp-level primitive can clarify which implementation to retain; whole-call timing alone does not isolate that cost.
memory_lessons.claim: The sync-intrinsic warp-reduction candidate was correct on 10 tested cases and averaged 30.015 µs; the generic shuffle variant was also correct and averaged 30.735 µs. These whole-call results do not establish the isolated cause of the timing difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this CTA-leader combination against the warp-0 reduction with the same mapping and launch/pass structure, and retain it as an alternative if it is correct even if it is slower.

proposal.hypothesis: Replacing warp 0's shuffle reduction of the four warp partials with a serial sum by thread 0 may reduce inter-warp combination instructions, but its dependent additions could instead cost more. This isolates the inter-warp combination while retaining the sync-intrinsic warp reduction, input mapping, 128-thread blocks, pass loop, and tail handling. The controller must measure the whole call; no speedup is claimed.

retained: Keep the one-element-per-thread global load and zero-pad out-of-range lanes so all launched warp lanes participate.
Reduce within each warp through the existing warpReduceSum helper using __activemask(); lane 0 stores one partial per warp in shared memory.
Use one __syncthreads() and have CTA thread 0 serially sum the warp partials, contrasting with a warp-0 partial reduction.
Leave run's 128-thread launch, pass loop, scratch selection, and output copy unchanged.
